correctness.rationale: The p-adic residue reduction is exact for all positive n when k>=2; CRT both constructs the period and excludes every omitted prime from any period. Counting CRT fibers gives the rational density. Finite-field image multiplicities prove coset invariance; Dirichlet-character orthogonality plus Pólya–Vinogradov yields an O_k((log p)^2/sqrt p) deviation uniformly in a. Exact verifier corroborated 33 full-period and 120 coset/mean cases, without substituting computation for the unrestricted proofs.

originality.rationale: The relevant recent and earlier primary gcd-floor polynomial studies require irrational coefficients. The rational linear precedent does not imply higher-degree coset/least-period classification. Broad literature, exact wording/alias/parameter searches, and competing stronger implications were checked; no identified result covers all four asserted claims. Unindexed prior equivalent work and an inaccessible original linear paper remain specified historical risks.

value.rationale: The exact least-period classification and rational density address a natural unexamined rational boundary of recent polynomial-floor gcd questions, while the coset spectrum and a uniform prime-denominator convergence theorem relate rational and irrational arithmetic statistics. Both the finite structural invariant and analytic transition carry mathematical use beyond routine example enumeration or a simple substitution; the work states the composite-denominator and growing-degree limitations.
